content.text:
The drawing shows a five-membered furan ring with an oxygen at the bottom and a CHO group attached at the top right.

Ring atoms, going around: O at the bottom, then a left carbon (C2), then an upper-left carbon (C3), then the upper-right carbon (C3'), then a right carbon (C2'). The CHO group sits on the upper-right carbon, which is the position adjacent to the carbon next to the oxygen. That makes it furan-3-carbaldehyde.

Double bonds: the left side has a double bond between the lower-left carbon and the upper-left carbon. The right side has a double bond between the upper-right carbon (bearing CHO) and the lower-right carbon. This is the normal furan pattern, with C2=C3 and C4=C5 in standard numbering.

Writing the SMILES from the aldehyde: O=Cc1ccoc1. The ring atoms are c1 (bearing CHO, position 3), c (position 4), c (position 5), o (position 1), and c1 (position 2). The CHO carbon is therefore at position 3, as drawn.

SMILES: O=Cc1ccoc1
